Challenge detection to stop-on-wall response flow
Compliance gating stack for risky sources
Cockpit control-plane request and live-update flow

nodes.label: JobLens Bounded Contexts
nodes.rationale: Sourcing (core) and Access & Politeness (supporting) get DDD; Insight & Export and Operations stay read models because they protect no invariants. Contexts communicate by IDs, not shared mutable entities.

nodes.label: Per-Source Circuit Breaker
nodes.rationale: Opens after 3 challenge/block failures in 24h or 2 consecutive blocks; cooldowns of 60 min (rate limit), 24h (challenge) and 7 days (repeated block). State is per source, not per profile, so a fresh profile cannot bypass a source-level block.

nodes.label: ContentHash
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 over stable fields only, excluding volatile data such as view counts; a changed hash is the only trigger for JobPostingUpdated.

nodes.label: DeduplicationPolicy
nodes.rationale: Identity plus stable content hash keeps one row per posting across searches while preserving FirstSeenAt and refreshing LastSeenAt.

nodes.label: JobPosting
nodes.rationale: Normalized deduplicated posting whose immutable identity is (SourceKey, ExternalJobId); Refresh updates mutable fields and ContentHash but never identity or FirstSeenAt, and absence from a search does not expire a posting in v1.

nodes.label: PolitenessPolicy
nodes.rationale: Computes uniform jittered delays within RunLimits, never returns less than the configured minimum, and relies on application-level one-request-at-a-time rather than sleeping in the domain.

nodes.label: QuotaPolicy
nodes.rationale: Checks persisted SourceQuota against per-source caps before the run and before each page/detail, returning Allowed or Exceeded.

nodes.label: RunEvent
nodes.rationale: Append-only audit/progress entity with monotonic sequence per run; payloads carry IDs and counts, never cookies or PII.

nodes.label: RunLimits
nodes.rationale: Value object enforcing hard caps: maxPages 1-30, maxJobs 1-1000, maxDetails 0-1000, minDelay >= 1s and <= maxDelay <= 2m. Caps are ceilings, not targets.

nodes.label: ScrapeRun
nodes.rationale: Aggregate root with a guarded lifecycle (Pending, StartingSession, Searching, Enriching, Persisting, PausedForChallenge, RateLimited, terminal states), monotonic stats and domain events per transition; terminal runs cannot transition again.

nodes.label: SearchProfile
nodes.rationale: Reusable validated search intent (source, keywords, locations, criteria, run limits, enabled flag); cannot be enabled for a HighRisk source without acknowledged consent.

nodes.label: SourceKey
nodes.rationale: Immutable lowercase source identifier (naukri/indeed/linkedin) that throws on unknown values, preventing typo-driven source drift.

nodes.label: SourceQuota
nodes.rationale: Per-source UTC-day counters (pages, details, runs, challenges) that never decrease within a day; caps come from options/policy, the entity stores only counts, and quota is persisted so restarts do not reset the day.

nodes.label: JobLens CLI Surface
nodes.rationale: Verbs doctor, db migrate, search create/list, session login/probe, scrape (with --dry-run/--no-enrich), runs list/show, export, source list, version; names may be refined in Phase 0 but verbs and behavior stay.

nodes.label: joblens doctor
nodes.rationale: Single diagnostic command for SDK/OS, Playwright browsers, Linux deps, paths/permissions, SQLite and pending migrations, config and compliance gates; also wraps browser installation to keep clean-machine setup under 15 minutes.

nodes.label: CLI Exit Codes
nodes.rationale: Distinct codes (0 success, 2 config, 3 paused for challenge, 4 rate limited, 5 circuit open, 6 parse failure, 130 cancelled) so schedulers do not treat a challenge as a crash or a rate limit as an immediate retry.

nodes.label: Cooldown Ladder
nodes.rationale: 429 -> stated Retry-After (30-60 min); JS challenge/CAPTCHA -> 45-60 min; second challenge -> 24h with reduced caps; third consecutive challenge -> 7 days or disable the source; 403 -> 24h minimum. Escalation encodes that repeated walls mean the approach, not the timing, is wrong.

nodes.label: Anti-Bot Metrics and Alerts
nodes.rationale: challenge_rate, block_rate, parse_failure_rate, retry_rate, pages/postings per run, session_age_days, time_to_first_posting and zero_result_streak, each with a threshold; any block is a stop-and-review event, not just a datapoint.

nodes.label: Retention Policy
nodes.rationale: Run artifacts 30 days (Storage:RetentionDays), logs 90 days via Serilog rolling, inactive postings 180 days (PostingRetentionDays), exports manual, profiles until reset.

nodes.label: OS Scheduling (cron/launchd/Task Scheduler)
nodes.rationale: Use the OS scheduler instead of an in-process daemon, with flock/launchd/Task Scheduler 'do not start a new instance' enforcing one run at a time; scheduling does not bypass compliance and a wall still exits without auto-retry.

nodes.label: Operator Security Checklist
nodes.rationale: Profiles 0700, no cookies/auth headers in logs or support bundles, no secrets in git, encrypted backups on shared disks, dependency scans, no live scraping or profiles in CI, local-only exports, retention cleanup, profiles never synced to cloud drives.

nodes.label: Artifacts Storage Layout
nodes.rationale: artifacts/{data/joblens.db, profiles/<source>/<engine>, runs/{runId}/{run.json,page-*.html,screenshot-*.png,trace.zip}, exports, logs, backups}; gitignored, profiles 0700 because they contain cookies.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting Matrix
nodes.rationale: Symptom-to-cause-to-fix table covering SDK/browser install, Linux deps, display issues, profile locks, Akamai/Cloudflare/auth walls, database locked, missing migrations, test discovery, WebKit deps and timezone/cookie problems.

nodes.label: TimeProvider and IRandomSource Injection
nodes.rationale: Domain/Application never call DateTime.Now or new Random(); injecting TimeProvider and IRandomSource keeps policies pure, tests deterministic and timestamps UTC.

nodes.label: Akamai Bot Manager
nodes.rationale: Observed as the Naukri wall via errors.edgesuite.net; unknown/headless sessions get a visible block page, so Naukri needs headed first contact and native pagination.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Bot Management
nodes.rationale: Indeed's managed challenge layer, reported in 2026 to challenge even the homepage within a handful of requests; treated as an access control to stop at, never to bypass.

nodes.label: Naukri Private Search API (jobapi/v3/search)
nodes.rationale: Reverse-engineered endpoint with an RSA nkparam token returning 20 cards with tagsAndSkills; fragile and unsupported, so it may only be an optional feature-flagged fast path with browser fallback after a time-boxed spike.

nodes.label: JobSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Typed, source-agnostic DTO extracted from a page before domain validation; the seam that lets parsers be tested offline and the domain stay free of HTML.

nodes.label: ChallengePolicy
nodes.rationale: Pure mapping from ChallengeKind to ChallengeDecision (continue, pause, manual pause, stop, open circuit, stop-and-inspect); CAPTCHA is never auto-solved and cooldown lengthens with consecutive challenges.

nodes.label: PageFingerprint
nodes.rationale: First external ID plus result-range text, used to detect that pagination actually advanced and prevent silent re-reading of the same page.

nodes.label: RetryPolicy
nodes.rationale: Retries only TransientError, max 2 attempts, exponential backoff plus jitter, honors Retry-After and never retries rate limits, challenges, CAPTCHA, login walls, access denial or source changes.

nodes.label: JobSourceContractTests
nodes.rationale: Shared abstract suite every IJobSource derives from, asserting stable lowercase key, declared capabilities, canonical URLs, correct job counts and that challenge fixtures are never extracted as jobs; no browser or network required.

nodes.label: Common Adapter Blueprint
nodes.rationale: Every adapter composes Consent/quota/circuit check -> URL build -> navigate/wait -> challenge? -> extract -> normalize/validate -> dedupe -> SearchPageResult -> optional enrichment, and ships UrlBuilder, parsers, classifier, capabilities, normalizer, fixtures and contract tests.

nodes.label: URL Canonicalization
nodes.rationale: Absolute https only, per-source host allowlist, strip utm_*/ref/src/trk/trackingId/fragments while keeping source-significant params (Indeed jk), reject javascript:/data:/credentials, cap length ~2048.

nodes.label: Indeed India Playbook
nodes.rationale: Restricted tier, disabled by default; Cloudflare-protected, so 1-2 pages with 12-25s delays, start increments of 10, no /graphql or private /api/ calls, and a stop with artifact on the first managed challenge.

nodes.label: Native Next Pagination (Naukri)
nodes.rationale: Naukri is an SPA: navigating directly to a -2 slug URL loses filter state, so the adapter must click the native Next control and poll until the page fingerprint changes, stopping if it does not.

nodes.label: Naukri Playbook
nodes.rationale: Standard tier, enabled by default, Akamai-protected; slug URL carries k/l/experience/jobAge, skills are read from cards to avoid detail visits, caps are 3 pages/60 jobs/60 details with 2.5-6s delays.

nodes.label: Selector Hit Logging
nodes.rationale: Logging Source/Field/Selector/FallbackIndex/Page per extraction makes DOM drift visible; a shift to fallback index 2+ is an early warning before a source breaks entirely.

nodes.label: Honeypot and Visibility Guards
nodes.rationale: Reject cards with display:none, visibility hidden/collapse, opacity < 0.15, aria-hidden, <=1px boxes, far off-screen positions, placeholder/non-allowlisted hrefs or hidden overlays; clicking a hidden trap is both bad data and a detection signal.

nodes.label: Error Taxonomy and Retry Rules
nodes.rationale: Only transient errors (timeouts, resets, 5xx) retry, max 2 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter; 403/429/CAPTCHA/challenge/auth-wall never retry because a retry storm turns a soft block into a ban.

nodes.label: Extraction Priority (JSON-LD first)
nodes.rationale: JSON-LD is most stable, semantic DOM is resilient, class substrings are logged fallbacks, and full-page text/regex is used only for salary/date - never identity. Every selector hit is logged so drift is visible before it breaks.

nodes.label: Result types for expected operational outcomes
nodes.norm_label: result types for expected operational outcomes

nodes.label: Stop-on-Wall Policy
nodes.rationale: On CAPTCHA, JS challenge, auth wall, 403 or 429 the run stops, captures screenshot/HTML/trace, cools down and requires a human. A wall is a stop signal, not a retry signal; retrying is how a soft block becomes a ban.

nodes.label: Playwright for .NET
nodes.rationale: Version 1.64.1; chosen over Selenium/Puppeteer for first-class .NET support, auto-wait locators, persistent contexts, tracing and network interception. Delivers Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, not real Safari.

nodes.label: Public Browser Diagnostics
nodes.rationale: FingerprintJS BotD, BrowserScan, CreepJS, Iphey, Sannysoft and DeviceAndBrowserInfo were used to measure exposure (not to 'pass'): headed scored 93-100 trust with hasCDP remaining true, headless was explicitly flagged.

nodes.label: WebKit Is Not Safari
nodes.rationale: Playwright's WebKit is a patched build, not Apple Safari; real Safari automation would need a separate SafariDriver adapter on macOS. Chromium is therefore the default production engine and Firefox/WebKit are compatibility/diagnostic targets.

nodes.label: xUnit.net v3
nodes.rationale: xunit.v3 4.0.2 with adapter 4.0.1; v2 is maintenance-only, while v3 offers an in-process runner, MTP support, assembly fixtures, TestContext, dynamic skip and an official Playwright PageTest package.

nodes.label: BrowserProfile
nodes.rationale: Persistent browser identity per source with engine/channel/locale/timezone and health states; cannot launch while CoolingDown before CooldownUntil or when ResetRequired, and needs 3 consecutive challenges to force a reset.

nodes.label: Local Fixture Server
nodes.rationale: Minimal ASP.NET Core static server inside E2E tests serving per-source search/detail/challenge pages on a random port, giving deterministic HTML, pagination, slow responses and challenge pages with no live-site or legal exposure.

nodes.label: Live Canary Tests
nodes.rationale: Category=Live, opt-in via JOBLENS_LIVE=1 with a real profile: one search page, no persistence, headed, stop on challenge. Never on every commit and excluded from coverage/release gates because live sites are flaky and rate-limited.

nodes.label: Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit.v3 PageTest
nodes.rationale: Official PageTest base class supplies Page/Context/Browser for E2E tests; use a custom BrowserFixture when a shared persistent context or specific profile is needed.

nodes.label: Browser Hygiene Defaults
nodes.rationale: Chromium bundled, headless false, genuine UA, en-IN, Asia/Kolkata, 1366x768, SlowMo 40ms, no extensions, permissions denied by default, optional static proxy only. Nothing about identity changes per request.

nodes.label: Inert Stealth Init Script
nodes.rationale: The legacy stealth script was a bare arrow-function string passed to add_init_script, so it never ran; had it run it would have made navigator.webdriver undefined, plugins a plain Array and permissions inconsistent - i.e. more detectable. The fix was deletion, and the policy is no spoofing ever.

nodes.label: Headed Persistent Browser Profile
nodes.rationale: Headed Chromium with a persistent user-data directory is materially lower-signal than headless: BotD flags headless, Naukri blocks headless, and an established cookie/history profile looks less suspicious. Headless is reserved for fixture E2E and diagnostics.

nodes.label: Consistency Beats Spoofing
nodes.rationale: Removing UA/language stubs raised BrowserScan from 44 to 100 and plugins were genuinely 5 rather than the script's 3; a stable genuine browser identity is less suspicious than a browser whose story changes per page.

nodes.label: .NET 10 LTS
nodes.rationale: LTS supported until 2028-11-14 while .NET 9 (STS only, ends 2026-11-10), .NET 8 (also ends 2026-11-10) and .NET 11 RC are rejected; cross-platform and matches the owner's ASP.NET Core experience. Revisit only for security/lifecycle reasons, not novelty.

nodes.label: global.json SDK pin (10.0.403, rollForward latestFeature)
nodes.rationale: Pins the SDK for reproducibility while allowing feature-band roll-forward; updated monthly after CI passes.

nodes.label: Clean Architecture layers (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Cli)
nodes.norm_label: clean architecture layers (domain, application, infrastructure, cli)
nodes.rationale: Domain holds pure aggregates/value objects/policies/events; Application holds use cases and ports; Infrastructure holds Playwright, EF Core, parsers, exporters; Cli is the composition root. No MediatR, AutoMapper, or generic repositories.

nodes.label: Focused (tactical) DDD for Sourcing and Access
nodes.norm_label: focused (tactical) ddd for sourcing and access
nodes.rationale: DDD is applied only where rules are complex (run lifecycle, session health, challenge policy, quotas, dedupe); Insight/Export use read models/query objects because DDD everywhere would over-model reporting. Event sourcing rejected in favour of the RunEvent audit trail.

nodes.label: Modular monolith
nodes.rationale: One user, one machine, three sources: microservices add ops overhead with no scale need, while CRUD buries run/session/challenge/quota/dedupe rules. One deployable, one SQLite writer, one browser session; testable core without browser/DB. Trade-off: layer discipline is mandatory, enforced by NetArchTest.

nodes.label: EF Core 10.0.14
nodes.rationale: Migrations and LINQ are familiar from ASP.NET Core; mappings stay provider-agnostic so PostgreSQL can be added behind the same repositories later. Dapper rejected as an extra layer since EF Core covers writes and read models.

nodes.label: SQLite as source of truth
nodes.rationale: Single-user local-first tool with thousands of postings, not millions; zero-ops single file, cross-platform, transactions and unique indexes for dedupe, and no server install burden. Trade-offs: single-writer concurrency, no multi-user network access, SQLite type affinities require real-SQLite tests, and large artifacts belong on the file system.

nodes.label: WAL single-writer configuration
nodes.rationale: WAL, foreign_keys=ON and busy_timeout plus one writer keep a local SQLite deployment reliable; backups use .backup rather than copying a live WAL database.

nodes.label: Unit of work per page batch
nodes.norm_label: unit of work per page batch

nodes.label: Four Detection Layers
nodes.rationale: Bot decisions draw on network/edge (IP, TLS, rate, WAF), browser (webdriver/CDP, headless markers, fingerprint, consistency), behaviour (mouse, dwell, honeypots) and session/server (cookies, account history, rules). CDP/TLS/IP residuals are unavoidable, so the goal is low volume and graceful stopping.

nodes.label: Detection Surface Matrix
nodes.rationale: Maps IP/ASN, TLS/HTTP2, browser, behaviour, session, server rules and content honeypots to whether JobLens can legitimately influence them; CDP and TLS residuals are accepted rather than spoofed.

nodes.label: Browser profile treated as a credential
nodes.norm_label: browser profile treated as a credential

nodes.label: JobLens v1 Phase Plan
nodes.rationale: Seven phases from foundation (Nov 2) to v1.0 (Dec 18) plus buffer, ~32 working days part-time; critical path is Phase 2 browser -> Phase 3 Naukri, with domain work overlapping spikes.

nodes.label: Central Package Management
nodes.rationale: One Directory.Packages.props with ManagePackageVersionsCentrally and transitive pinning keeps every project on the verified versions (Playwright 1.64.1, xUnit 4.0.2, EF Core 10.0.14).

nodes.label: global.json SDK Pin
nodes.rationale: SDK 10.0.403 with rollForward latestFeature and allowPrerelease false gives reproducible local/CI behavior without falling back to an older SDK.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge-Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Agents must query the committed graph before grepping or reading source, use graphify path/explain for scoped answers, and run 'graphify update .' after code changes, because a scoped subgraph is smaller and cheaper than raw grep or GRAPH_REPORT.md. Dirty graph artifacts are expected and are not a reason to skip the graph.

nodes.label: AngleSharp
nodes.rationale: CSS-selector HTML parsing for offline fixtures and server-rendered pages, so parsers can be unit-tested without a browser.

nodes.label: ClosedXML
nodes.rationale: Cross-platform Excel export with hyperlinks and no Office dependency.

nodes.label: Pre-Phase Spikes S1-S7
nodes.rationale: Each spike is time-boxed and produces a written note plus fixture; S1-S3 are research only and hitting a wall during a spike means record and stop, not bypass.

nodes.label: System.CommandLine
nodes.rationale: 2.0.14, stable and testable CLI parsing without a heavy framework.

nodes.label: xUnit.net v3
nodes.rationale: xUnit v2 is maintenance-only; v3 is the active line with stand-alone executables, Microsoft Testing Platform support, assembly fixtures, TestContext, dynamic skip, MatrixTheoryData and official Playwright integration. Costs: test projects must be Exe, ValueTask IAsyncLifetime, and VSTest vs MTP mode must be chosen consistently in CI.

nodes.label: Playwright for .NET
nodes.rationale: Target sites are JS-heavy and anti-bot protected; Playwright .NET 1.64.1 gives one .NET API for Chromium/Firefox/WebKit with auto-wait, persistent contexts, tracing and codegen, and the owner knows C#/.NET rather than a Node-first stack. Trade-offs: WebKit is not real Safari, Firefox is a patched build, browser binaries are version-coupled, and CDP/automation signals stay detectable.

nodes.label: Optional Naukri API fast path (jobapi/v3/search with RSA nkparam)
nodes.norm_label: optional naukri api fast path (jobapi/v3/search with rsa nkparam)
nodes.rationale: Feature-flagged and off by default; enabled only after a time-boxed spike proves it stable/compliant, always falling back to the browser, and disabled on 403/406. The private API is never allowed to bypass a wall, login, or rate limit.

nodes.label: Per-source compliance tiers and consent gates
nodes.norm_label: per-source compliance tiers and consent gates
nodes.rationale: Sources carry different legal terms and bot defences, so risk is tiered per source; LinkedIn is high-risk and disabled by default unless explicitly approved.

nodes.label: Manual/nightly live canaries (never in CI)
nodes.rationale: Detects fixture drift from real sites without exposing CI to flakiness, rate limits or legal/ethical risk; opt-in and separated from the merge gate.

nodes.label: Local fixture server for Playwright E2E
nodes.norm_label: local fixture server for playwright e2e
nodes.rationale: Keeps browser tests fast, deterministic and legal while still exercising integration, waits and selectors; fixtures stay minimal/synthetic and must be refreshed against real sites.

nodes.label: Risk-based coverage gates (Domain 95/90, Application 90/85, overall 85/80)
nodes.rationale: The old project's 100% gate was expensive and did not prove behavior; gates are weighted toward the failure modes that matter (challenge, rate limit, dedupe, cancellation) and coverage reflects risk, not vanity.

nodes.label: Bundled Chromium default browser (D9)
nodes.rationale: Lowest install friction, pinned and cross-platform; Chrome/Edge/Firefox/WebKit stay available via --engine/--channel for diagnostics, and real Safari is never promised.

nodes.label: CSV + Excel export (JSON optional, Postgres later)
nodes.norm_label: csv + excel export (json optional, postgres later)
nodes.rationale: Excel hyperlinks are the primary human workflow and both formats are universal; Parquet/Postgres are overkill for personal volume, and the export port keeps them addable later.

nodes.label: Data retention 30/90/180 days (D12)
nodes.rationale: Artifacts 30 days, logs 90 days, postings 180 days since last seen (configurable), exports user-managed, profiles until reset; balances privacy against storage and is enforced by a joblens cleanup command.

nodes.label: Full posting field set (D4)
nodes.rationale: Includes source, external job ID, canonical/apply URL, title, company, location raw+normalized, work mode, experience, salary raw+parsed, posted date, description, snippet, skills, first/last seen, content hash, status and data-quality flags. Recruiter names/emails/phones, profiles, application answers and interview reviews are excluded in v1; the field set drives schema, parsers and exports.

nodes.label: Indeed opt-in with conservative caps (D3)
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare managed challenge blocks appear within a handful of requests and headless is often challenged; opt-in avoids a poor first-run experience and forces explicit risk acceptance. Caps: 2 pages, 40 jobs, 12-25s delay, 1 run/day.

nodes.label: JobLens working project name (D1)
nodes.rationale: Short and descriptive with namespaces JobLens.*; a trademark/package/repo search is required before a public release, and renaming is a mechanical find/replace.

nodes.label: LinkedIn opt-in high-risk, default disabled (D2)
nodes.rationale: LinkedIn robots.txt and the User Agreement prohibit automated scraping, auth wall/429/999 appear quickly and login automation raises account risk. Recommended: adapter exists but disabled by default with explicit acknowledgment, guest-only, one page, stop on wall; the architecture does not depend on LinkedIn.

nodes.label: Normal network egress, no rotation (D8)
nodes.rationale: Lowest legal/detection risk; a single user-supplied static residential proxy is acceptable for geo consistency if locale/timezone match, but rotation pools are out of policy as evasion.

nodes.label: Recruiter emails/profiles out of scope (D10)
nodes.rationale: Avoids DPDP/GDPR and LinkedIn ToS exposure plus data-quality/scope creep; if added later it needs its own bounded context, privacy assessment, consent basis and retention.

nodes.label: Challenge handoff to host headed browser
nodes.norm_label: challenge handoff to host headed browser
nodes.rationale: The API emits run.challenge with kind, evidence, cooldown and artifact IDs; the UI shows a blocking alert and the operator solves it in the headed browser on the host, then probes or resumes. The cockpit never solves, retries or bypasses, and challenge/403/429 retries are forbidden.

nodes.label: Phase 0 open decisions (D1-D12 with recommended defaults)
nodes.norm_label: phase 0 open decisions (d1-d12 with recommended defaults)
nodes.rationale: Unblocks Phase 0 (target first commit 2026-11-02): if the owner does not choose, the recommendation is used, and the architecture is designed to keep the blast radius of later changes small.

nodes.label: Headed first contact + persistent contexts per source
nodes.norm_label: headed first contact + persistent contexts per source
nodes.rationale: Persistent contexts keep cookies/session state and headed first contact lowers detection signalling per source; never add fingerprint-spoofing packages.

nodes.label: Browser-first automation as source of truth
nodes.norm_label: browser-first automation as source of truth
nodes.rationale: Raw HTTP fails on JS challenges and exposes a TLS/HTTP fingerprint that does not match the claimed browser; a single browser path works across JS/SPA pages and survives API rotation/outage. Cost: slower, more resource usage, more moving parts. IJobSource stays the seam for a future adapter.

nodes.label: Compliance-first low-signal automation policy
nodes.rationale: Headed persistent Chromium measured low-signal while headless is flagged and CDP/TLS/network signals remain detectable; LinkedIn explicitly prohibits automated access, Indeed is Cloudflare-protected. Policy: genuine UA/locale/timezone, human pacing, strict caps, one run at a time, stop on walls, no CAPTCHA solving/proxy rotation/account rotation/auth-wall bypass/retry storms. Trade-off: lower throughput, manual intervention, not undetectable.

nodes.label: Stop-on-wall with manual challenge solve
nodes.rationale: Retrying through 403/429 turns a soft block into a ban, so walls are detected and the run stops for manual solving; artifacts are captured on every wall and caps/quota/circuit breakers are enforced in code, not docs.

nodes.label: Test pyramid
nodes.rationale: Deterministic logic (URL builders, parsers, policies) dominates, while live-site tests are slow, flaky, rate-limited and legally risky in CI. Layers: many domain/application unit tests, parser tests with saved HTML fixtures, adapter contract tests, real-file SQLite integration tests, a small Playwright E2E suite against a local fixture server, and manual/nightly live canaries.

nodes.label: Deferred API/dashboard (post-Phase 3)
nodes.rationale: Deferred until after the Naukri vertical slice and only if a real need appears; read-only endpoints first, scraping logic never in controllers. Refined by ADR-0010, which promotes the API to the first v2.0 deliverable for the cockpit.

nodes.label: Same-origin Bun BFF
nodes.rationale: The BFF proxies /api/v1/* and /events/* to the loopback .NET API, injects the bearer token, serves the SPA, owns the auth cookie/CSRF and normalizes SSE. This removes CORS, keeps the API token out of the browser, gives one cookie model and lets the browser never call the .NET API or any job site directly. Cost: another process and another place for auth bugs, so it must stay small, tested and loopback-only.

nodes.label: React + Bun web cockpit (v2.0)
nodes.rationale: The operator needs a central control system (health, profiles, runs, challenges, jobs, exports, diagnostics). Building it promotes the .NET API from deferred to the first v2.0 deliverable, growing v2 scope while v1 stays CLI-only. Bun is younger than Node and shadcn components are copy-in code, so W0 must prove the toolchain.

nodes.label: shadcn/ui copy-in components
nodes.rationale: The shadcn CLI copies component source into the repo, so components are owned source rather than an opaque dependency and the UI can be dense and keyboard-first; upgrades are manual diffs pinned by CLI version.

nodes.label: HTTP/JSON commands + Server-Sent Events transport
nodes.rationale: SSE gives a live cockpit without bidirectional socket complexity; WebSocket is revisited only if bidirectional terminal/log interaction becomes a real requirement.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
nodes.rationale: Lightweight ADRs capture why a decision was made, the alternatives and the consequences; they are immutable once accepted and a later ADR supersedes an earlier one. Conventions: Status (Proposed/Accepted/Superseded/Deprecated), ISO 8601 Date, Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives, sequential numbering and index links.

nodes.label: OS scheduler for scheduling (D6)
nodes.rationale: cron/launchd/Task Scheduler is simple, reliable and survives app crashes with no daemon; a hosted scheduler is added only if a dashboard/API needs it.

nodes.label: Cockpit auth: loopback bind, HttpOnly cookie, CSRF double-submit, BFF bearer token
nodes.norm_label: cockpit auth: loopback bind, httponly cookie, csrf double-submit, bff bearer token
nodes.rationale: A 32-byte token is printed once and stored only as an Argon2id hash in ~/.config/joblens/cockpit.token (0600); login sets joblens_session (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict) and a readable joblens_csrf cookie verified on mutations with an Origin check. 12h idle / 7d absolute expiry; JOBLENS_API_TOKEN is server-only and never logged; remote access is off by default and needs an explicit flag plus TLS.

nodes.label: Bun BFF runtime (Bun.serve, /api/v1 proxy, SSE proxy, static hosting)
nodes.norm_label: bun bff runtime (bun.serve, /api/v1 proxy, sse proxy, static hosting)
nodes.rationale: A same-origin Bun.serve process that serves dist/client with SPA fallback, proxies /api/v1/* to JOBLENS_API_URL injecting the bearer token, streams text/event-stream with Last-Event-ID passthrough and buffering disabled, owns cookie/CSRF/security headers, generates X-Request-Id and enforces body/timeout/login limits. This is why the browser never calls the .NET API directly: no CORS, no token in the browser, one cookie model.

nodes.label: Bun native package manager (bun install/bun ci, bun.lock, minimumReleaseAge)
nodes.norm_label: bun native package manager (bun install/bun ci, bun.lock, minimumreleaseage)
nodes.rationale: One lockfile (bun.lock) and resolver for dev/CI/release; bun ci is a frozen-lockfile install used in CI and release, lifecycle scripts are blocked by default via trustedDependencies, and minimumReleaseAge = 3d is a supply-chain guard. npm/npx/yarn/pnpm/Corepack are never invoked, and node_modules still exists because only the Node runtime is banned.

nodes.label: Web cockpit (v2 control plane)
nodes.rationale: A local web application that commands the .NET API to run scraping, monitoring, exports and diagnostics: dashboard, sources, search profiles, runs, jobs, sessions, diagnostics and a command palette. It never scrapes, launches a browser or talks to job sites, and it is a view/command surface only - SQLite in .NET stays authoritative.

nodes.label: CSP and security headers
nodes.rationale: Strict same-origin CSP (script-src 'self', frame-ancestors none, base-uri none) plus nosniff, no-referrer, Permissions-Policy, COOP/CORP. style-src 'unsafe-inline' is a pragmatic React/shadcn allowance; script-src 'unsafe-inline' is never added. Artifacts are download-only to prevent XSS via scraped HTML.

nodes.label: Cockpit delivery plan W0-W4
nodes.rationale: W0 spike and contract, W1 shell and read-only, W2 commands and live runs, W3 sessions/exports/diagnostics, W4 hardening: roughly 16-20 working days after the API contract. It is a v2.0 track and does not change the v1.0 CLI date; W0 can start in parallel with Phase 3 against a stub API.

nodes.label: .NET API command surface (/api/v1)
nodes.rationale: JSON-only UTF-8 with ISO 8601 UTC, opaque string IDs, RFC 9457 Problem Details, loopback bind plus bearer token from the BFF, no CORS, 202 Accepted for long-running work and idempotent commands. Endpoints cover health/doctor, sources, search profiles, runs, artifacts, jobs, exports, sessions, quotas and metrics.

nodes.label: openapi-typescript generated contracts
nodes.rationale: The .NET OpenAPI 3.1 document is the single source of truth: openapi-typescript writes src/shared/contracts.ts, CI regenerates and fails on drift, and openapi-fetch adds a middleware for the CSRF header and Problem Details mapping.

nodes.label: Cockpit performance budgets
nodes.rationale: Initial JS <=250KB gzip excluding charts, route chunk <=120KB, dashboard LCP <=2.0s, command round-trip <=150ms p95, SSE-to-UI <=50ms p95, 10,000-row jobs table via server pagination plus virtualization, idle tab <=150MB. Achieved through route-level splitting, lazy charts/diagnostics, virtualized tables and SSE-driven invalidation.

nodes.label: Run lifecycle stages (Pending to Completed/Cancelled)
nodes.rationale: Pending -> StartingSession -> Searching -> Enriching -> Persisting -> Completed, with PausedForChallenge and RateLimited branches, Failed, and Cancelling -> Cancelled from any non-terminal state. The UI renders the domain stages verbatim because RunStage is the contract; inventing a parallel status model is forbidden.

nodes.label: SSE run event stream (run.* / session / quota / export events)
nodes.norm_label: sse run event stream (run.* / session / quota / export events)
nodes.rationale: Server-authoritative events with monotonic per-run sequence, bounded replay buffer and Last-Event-ID resume, 15s heartbeat, exponential backoff with jitter and polling fallback after two failures. run.posting is batched at most once per page to avoid render storms; the UI never guesses a terminal state.

nodes.label: Tailwind CSS v4 CSS-first configuration
nodes.rationale: No tailwind.config.js: globals.css imports tailwindcss, tw-animate-css and shadcn/tailwind.css with @theme tokens. The official @tailwindcss/cli is used instead of Bun's native bun-plugin-tailwind because that plugin is not an official Tailwind release and can lag the pinned version.

nodes.label: TanStack Query state model with SSE cache updates
nodes.norm_label: tanstack query state model with sse cache updates
nodes.rationale: Server data lives in TanStack Query, live events flow through an SSE reducer into the query cache, filters/sort/page live in URL search params, form drafts in react-hook-form, and auth in an HttpOnly cookie. No Zustand/Redux mirror of server data, no second run store, optimistic updates only for UI-only toggles because run state is server-authoritative.

nodes.label: CLI-first (System.CommandLine + Hosting + Serilog)
nodes.rationale: One developer on one machine; an API/dashboard would add endpoints, auth, hosting, CORS, UI and tests before the collection pipeline is proven. CLI gives the smallest useful surface, easy OS scheduling, first-class logs/artifacts, and no auth/hosting/UI scope creep; Application stays independent of the CLI so handlers are reusable by a later API.

nodes.label: No Node.js policy
nodes.rationale: Bun 1.4.4 replaces node/npm/npx/yarn/pnpm, Vite/webpack, Jest/Vitest, Prettier/Biome and ts-node, removing four or five dependencies and their configs. Node-targeted CLIs are run via bunx --bun so Node is never installed; node_modules still exists, only the Node runtime is absent.

nodes.label: Data plane (.NET) vs control plane (cockpit) split
nodes.norm_label: data plane (.net) vs control plane (cockpit) split
nodes.rationale: The .NET engine owns Playwright sessions, adapters, API clients, parsing, persistence, quotas and compliance policy; the cockpit only observes and commands. Hard rule: every policy, cap, consent gate and stop-on-wall decision is enforced by the .NET API and the UI cannot override it.

nodes.label: v1 Success Criteria
nodes.rationale: Success is measured by low challenge/block rates and graceful stops, not by claiming invisibility; includes cross-OS build, <15 min onboarding, Naukri end-to-end, LinkedIn refusal without consent, 100% challenge-fixture detection and coverage gates.

nodes.label: SQLite + EF Core 10
nodes.rationale: Zero-ops single-file local database with transactions and easy backup, sufficient for one user; PostgreSQL remains a later option behind provider-agnostic EF Core code.

nodes.label: CI Pipeline
nodes.rationale: restore -> build -warnaserror -> unit -> integration -> contract -> architecture -> E2E fixtures (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit) -> coverage/TRX -> artifacts; Ubuntu runs E2E every commit, Windows/macOS smaller matrix and nightly full browser matrix; never live scraping.

nodes.label: Coverage Gates
nodes.rationale: Risk-based thresholds: Domain 95/90, Application 90/85, Infrastructure 70/60, CLI 70/60, overall 85/80; E2E excluded. 100% coverage is explicitly rejected as a vanity target.

nodes.label: SQLite Backup and Restore
nodes.rationale: Use sqlite3 .backup rather than copying a live WAL database, verify with PRAGMA integrity_check, store encrypted if personal data, back up before every migration and never restore profiles and DB from different dates.

nodes.label: Release Checklist
nodes.rationale: Green cross-OS build/tests/E2E matrix, coverage gates, no critical vulns or secrets, doctor clean on macOS+Linux, self-contained publishes for osx-arm64/linux-x64/win-x64, documented canaries, runbook/playbooks updated, backup-restore drill passed, tag v1.0.0.

nodes.label: Monthly Upgrade Procedure
nodes.rationale: Back up, review .NET/Playwright/xUnit/EF Core notes, update pins intentionally, build/test, reinstall browsers together with Playwright, run the E2E matrix and a one-page canary, then update docs; rollback via previous artifact plus backup, never by editing an applied migration.

nodes.label: Deliberately Absent Packages
nodes.rationale: MediatR, AutoMapper, FluentValidation, Polly, Dapper, Selenium, FluentAssertions, Moq and any stealth/undetected package are excluded: explicit handlers/mapping/guards and a small tested retry policy are enough, several carry license ambiguity, and stealth tooling is out of policy.

nodes.label: Flaky Test Policy
nodes.rationale: No blind retries: a retry hides a race or bad selector. Reproduce, capture trace/screenshot, fix the root cause, otherwise quarantine with owner and expiry; quarantined tests cannot count toward release gates.

nodes.label: Test Pyramid
nodes.rationale: Many fast domain/application unit tests, some parser/contract/integration tests, and a few browser E2E tests against a local fixture server; if a test can be written one level lower it should be, because browser tests are slow and nondeterministic.

nodes.label: v1 Scope Boundary
nodes.rationale: In scope: public search/detail pages, normalized postings, enrichment, analysis, CSV/Excel export, run history. Out of scope: auto-apply, recruiter email harvesting, CAPTCHA solving, fingerprint spoofing, proxy rotation, auth-wall bypass, multi-tenant SaaS and ML ranking, because those are a different risk class or add no value for one user.

nodes.label: Anti-ban by being a good citizen
nodes.norm_label: anti-ban by being a good citizen

nodes.label: Hard exclusions (no CAPTCHA solving, no spoofing)
nodes.norm_label: hard exclusions (no captcha solving, no spoofing)

nodes.label: CompliancePolicy
nodes.rationale: Pure truth table deciding CanRun, RequiresManualSession and AllowedCapabilities per compliance tier; HighRisk needs acknowledgment plus config flag plus manual confirmation.

nodes.label: ComplianceTier
nodes.rationale: Standard/Restricted/HighRisk classification that drives consent and run gates; Naukri Standard, Indeed Restricted, LinkedIn HighRisk.

nodes.label: One polite pass at a time
nodes.norm_label: one polite pass at a time

nodes.label: .NET 10 LTS
nodes.rationale: SDK 10.0.403 / runtime 10.0.14, supported to 2028-11-14; chosen for the long support window, cross-platform self-contained publish, C# 14, TimeProvider and the operator's existing C#/ASP.NET Core skills.

nodes.label: JobLens
nodes.rationale: Working product name for a cross-platform .NET 10 job-board automation and public job-posting collector for Naukri, Indeed India and opt-in LinkedIn; planning complete, implementation not started.
